window._about:
Truncation-free check of the age effect (student's question, 11 Oct).

Window sample: papers published early enough to have W full years of follow-up before the 2025-12-31 completeness
cutoff (publication date <= 2025-12-31 minus W years), and retractions within W years of publication (calendar years;
29 Feb + W years -> 28 Feb, same as R's %m+%). Every paper in the window sample had the same W-year chance to be
retracted, so the ceiling cannot create an age effect: what is left of log_age is a real cohort difference.

Same 9-term formula as the report's model, fitted to the window sample within each of the 16 whisk states
(the refit rule: population groups refit). Inference: batch (publisher x retraction-date) bootstrap, 2,000 reps,
p from t = beta / SE_boot with (batches - 1) df; CR1 sandwich as cross-check.
Also (default state, W = 3): publication-year effects holding the other 8 terms fixed (cohort dummies, 2010 = reference),
and the case-type composition of each cohort.

Run: ../.venv/bin/python window_check.py -> out/window_check.json, out/window_flags.csv ; independent route: Rscript window_check.R
window._about_g5: G5 = Hindawi papers (publisher == Hindawi), shown by default. Keys without a suffix show them (9 terms); keys ending in _G5off hide them, and the constant hindawi term is dropped (8 terms; see terms_final).

W3_singles_default.note: individually handled: not in a same-day publisher batch of 10+ (batch size counted on all rows, as in Trends)

cohorts_default_W3.note: adj_days = predicted days for a paper with the other 8 terms at the window-sample means; 95% bootstrap interval

about.method: Nonparametric estimator for right-truncated waits (Lagakos, Barraj & De Gruttola 1988), the continuous form of the actuarial chain ladder. future(year) = sum over that year's retracted papers of 1/F(T) - 1, T = days from publication to 2026-09-11.
assumptions: the wait distribution is the same for every publication year
no retraction comes later than the longest wait observable in the data
about.interval: 90% percentile interval, batch bootstrap (publisher x retraction-date batches resampled), B = 500, seed = state index
